story.headline: RL for LLMs wastes compute on easy problems
story.summary: A never-give-up adaptive sampler reallocates RL compute from easy to hard problems.
story.display_body: Reinforcement learning (RL — training a model by rewarding correct answers) improves an LLM far more on problems it can already usually solve than on genuinely hard ones — a pattern the authors name the "Matthew effect" (the rich get richer). They argue standard RL squanders compute re-solving easy problems, and introduce Never Give Up (NGU): keep sampling a problem until a correct answer appears, then, using asynchronous RL, spend fewer samples on the easy problems and pour the freed budget into the hard ones.
story.why: Frontier RL runs are enormously expensive, and this reframes part of that spend as misallocated rather than merely insufficient — a scheduling change, not more GPUs, closes some of the hard-problem gap.

story.headline: Fully open 7B model leans on tools not memorization
story.summary: ZGCM-1 is a from-scratch open 7B dense model for math and agentic search over 256K context.
story.display_body: ZGCM-1 is a 7-billion-parameter dense model trained from scratch with a fully open recipe, on the premise that a small model cannot memorize the open web but can compensate by pairing internal reasoning with external tool use (search, code) over a 256K-token context. The recipe combines an interleaved sliding-window/full-attention design, an FP8 Muon optimizer, and a staged curriculum that scales context from 16K to 256K and recasts tool-interaction traces as Markov decision processes (a formalism for sequential decisions) during mid-training.
story.why: Open, reproducible recipes for capable small models are scarce — most frontier work is closed — so a from-scratch, documented 7B aimed at math and agentic search lowers the barrier to study and build on. The paper is bylined to an unnamed "ZGCM Team" and the efficiency claims are the authors' own; treat them as unverified until independently reproduced.

story.headline: Reasoning models fail logical twins of solved tasks
story.summary: Reasoning models fail structurally equivalent variants of rule-induction tasks they can solve.
story.display_body: "Systematicity" is the principle that understanding a concept implies understanding close variations of it. The authors take rule-induction tasks from cognitive science and build structurally equivalent variants — the same underlying rule, recombined or with symbols substituted — then check whether a model that solves one variant also solves its isomorphs. Often it does not: models fail variants that are logically identical to problems they just got right.
story.why: It is direct evidence that apparent reasoning can be brittle and non-compositional — getting a benchmark item right does not mean the model has grasped the rule behind it, which bears on any use that assumes it will generalize.

story.headline: Cheaper training-data attribution at model scale
story.summary: Budgeted data attribution recast as estimating an influence matrix from few measurements.
story.display_body: Data attribution measures how much each training example shaped a given prediction — the basis for data valuation, machine unlearning (removing a datapoint's influence after the fact), and interpretability. Exact "metagradient" methods such as MAGIC differentiate through the whole training run but need a separate run per prediction, which is prohibitive. This work recasts budgeted attribution as estimating a large "influence matrix" from a small number of measurements, and shows which measurements best recover it.
story.why: If influence can be approximated from a few measurements instead of one run per query, attribution becomes tractable at model scale — practical for unlearning requests, copyright and data-valuation disputes, and debugging which data drove a behavior. (MAGIC co-author Andrew Ilyas is on the paper.)

story.headline: Diagnosing agent failures as a search problem
story.summary: Root-cause attribution of long-horizon agent failures reframed as continual trace search.
story.display_body: Long-horizon AI agents produce huge execution logs, and the true cause of a failure is often a single early action far from where things visibly broke. Existing root-cause methods hand an LLM the whole trace and ask for a one-shot verdict, which degrades as traces grow and relevant clues become sparse and scattered. The authors reframe diagnosis as a search problem — continually searching the trace for the responsible step rather than committing to an early guess.
story.why: Reliable agents need to turn "it failed" into "it failed here, because of this", and one-shot judging does not scale to long traces; treating attribution as search is a route to debugging that holds up as agents run longer.

story.headline: When an interrupted agent can safely resume
story.summary: Recoverability as a system primitive binding agent state reuse to evidence and checks.
story.display_body: Agents get interrupted mid-task; restarting repeats completed work, but blindly continuing from a saved state can carry forward unverified or stale progress. The paper introduces "recoverability" as an explicit system primitive: a saved state is paired with a permitted recovery action and a contract binding that choice to supporting evidence and independent checks, so resuming is a deliberate decision rather than an automatic one. Their challenge set shows accurate-looking restoration can quietly hide disallowed reuse.
story.why: As agents run longer and touch real files and tools, "resume from checkpoint" becomes a correctness question, not just a convenience — this frames the safeguards a runtime needs before it trusts its own saved state.

story.headline: A DSL compiling attention variants to fused GPU kernels
story.summary: AttnFuse makes pre-multiplication transforms like RoPE first-class for fused attention kernels.
story.display_body: Attention dominates transformer compute, and every new attention variant normally needs hand-written GPU code to run at usable speed. PyTorch's flex_attention lets researchers describe custom attention in Python but only handles changes applied after the core matrix multiply — which excludes RoPE (rotary position embedding, the positional scheme used by every major LLM), because RoPE acts before it. AttnFuse is a domain-specific language that makes such pre-multiplication transforms first-class, composing ten high-level building blocks into fused kernels.
story.why: Lowering the cost of turning a new attention idea into production-speed code shortens the loop between architecture research and usable models — and it targets exactly the gap (RoPE) that existing tooling left open.

story.headline: Scoring attention edits exactly from one backward pass
story.summary: Exact local attention responses to positional edits from a cached baseline and one backward pass.
story.display_body: This is an interpretability-and-editing result: it derives the exact local response of attention to a positional intervention, so a candidate edit can be scored from a cached baseline plus one backward pass instead of re-running the model. Starting from how attention output changes with position (the RoPE derivative), it carries the displacement through the softmax without linearizing, and it keeps the interaction term when keys and values are edited together — a cross effect naive attributions drop. It reports ~95–96% sign accuracy across 92,160 positional edits.
story.why: Cheap, exact scoring of "what if I nudged this position or token?" makes attention-level interpretability and targeted editing far more practical, and it shows the cross term that separate attributions ignore is not negligible.

story.headline: One framework for policy iteration and self-improvement
story.summary: Generalized Agent Iteration formalizes iterative policy improvement and recursive self-improvement as one paradigm.
story.display_body: Recursive self-improvement (RSI — a system getting better at making itself better) is invoked loosely and has no agreed formal description, unlike its classical cousin, generalized policy iteration, where the improvement rule sits outside the agent. Generalized Agent Iteration (GAI) treats the agent as a configuration of modifiable components and models learning as updates to those components, casting ordinary iterative policy improvement and RSI as two cases of a single paradigm.
story.why: A precise vocabulary for what "self-improving AI" actually means helps separate genuine mechanisms from hype — useful for judging which RSI claims are substantive.

story.headline: ElevenLabs ships Music v2.5
story.summary: ElevenLabs released Music v2.5 as the default model in ElevenMusic with new ownership terms.
story.display_body: ElevenLabs makes Music v2.5 the default in its music app. ElevenLabs released Music v2.5, now the default for both prompted and reference-based generation in ElevenMusic. The company claims more layered, complex songs and more natural-sounding instruments, and spells out ownership terms: users own what they make on every tier including Free (five lossless downloads/day; Pro 400/month), while downloads are blocked on tracks that reference other artists' songs.

story.headline: OpenAI details billion-user storage platform
story.summary: OpenAI describes scaling its Habitat storage to serve over a billion ChatGPT users.
story.display_body: OpenAI details the storage platform behind a billion ChatGPT users. In an engineering post, OpenAI describes how it evolved its "Habitat" storage from a Python library into a globally distributed platform serving roughly a billion ChatGPT users at about 22 million requests per second. It is infrastructure, not a model release, but a rare concrete look at production scale.

story.headline: Edge0 runs a 35B MoE in phone-class memory
story.summary: Edge0-35B-A3B is an MLX open-weights MoE running in ~3 GiB active RAM via SSD expert offload.
story.display_body: Edge0-35B-A3B-preview is an open-weights sparse MoE (mixture-of-experts — only a few of many "expert" sub-networks fire per token; here 4 of 256), post-built on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B and shipped for the edge0 MLX streaming framework. Its pitch is memory: by streaming experts off SSD, it claims to run in under 3 GiB of active RAM at ~15 tokens/second decode in 4-bit, with a recovery-LoRA distillation step that keeps int4 quality within ~3.9 points of the fp16 base. Apache-2.0, with a smaller 8B-A1B preview alongside.

story.headline: XHToken releases Spark-X2.5 compact agentic models
story.summary: Spark-X2.5 ships 4B and 1.7B Apache-2.0 agentic models with native 1M-token context.
story.display_body: XHToken releases Spark-X2.5, compact agentic models with a 1M-token context. Spark-X2.5 ships in 4B and 1.7B sizes (Apache-2.0), using a hybrid attention layout (one full-attention layer per three sliding-window layers) to reach a native 1-million-token context across 200+ languages, and is wired to run inside agent harnesses like Codex and Claude Code.

story.headline: Nex-AGI launches Nex-N2.5 agentic model family
story.summary: Nex-AGI released the Nex-N2.5 mini/Pro/Max agentic family, Max a 1.6T-parameter MoE.
story.display_body: Nex-AGI released Nex-N2.5 in three sizes (mini, Pro, Max). Pro builds on its Nex-N2 multimodal foundation with gains in computer use, web browsing and visually grounded agentic tasks, while the Max tier is a 1.6-trillion-parameter text-only MoE — the group's first trillion-scale post-training. Apache-2.0. Capability claims are the vendor's own and unaudited here.

story.headline: M-A-P releases YuE2 open music model with editable scores
story.summary: YuE2-3B is an open text-to-audio music model with symbolic planning and editable scores.
story.display_body: M-A-P releases YuE2, an open music model with editable scores. YuE2-3B is a 3B open text-to-audio music model from the multimodal-art-projection group, built around symbolic planning and agentic editing so a generated song can be revised at the score level rather than regenerated wholesale. story.headline: Microsoft publishes Humanist AI Code of Conduct
story.summary: Microsoft AI published a code of conduct on readable model thinking, no inner life, and no AI rights.
story.display_body: Microsoft publishes a "Humanist AI Code of Conduct". Microsoft AI released a code of conduct staking out an explicit position in the AI-welfare debate: per the document and secondary coverage, it calls for models whose "thinking" is legible to people, states that AI systems have no inner life, and rules out AI rights. It is a values statement rather than a product or policy change, but a notable public stance from a frontier lab as questions of model "welfare" gain attention.

story.headline: Anthropic reportedly eyes a Nasdaq listing
story.summary: The FT reports Anthropic is weighing a Nasdaq listing after a claimed second profitable quarter.
story.display_body: The FT reports Anthropic is weighing a Nasdaq listing. The Financial Times reported that Anthropic is eyeing a Nasdaq listing and, per the report, is pointing to a claimed second profitable quarter to court investors ahead of a possible large IPO. This is reporting, not an Anthropic announcement, and the underlying financials are attributed to sources rather than confirmed filings — treat it as a signal of intent, not a done deal.
